chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Any man who is killed by the legal penalty (Hadd) in retaliation (Qisas), there is no wergild (Diyah) for him.
And he said: Any man who attacks another man to strike him, and he defends himself against him, injuring him or killing him, there is nothing upon him (no compensation).
And he said: Any man who peers at a people in their house to look at their private parts, and they pelt him, blinding his eyes or injuring him, there is no wergild for them.
And he said: Whoever initiates (an attack) and exceeds (in it), and is attacked against, there is no retaliation (Qawd) for him.

key_terms.الْقِصَاص: Retaliation (in kind) for murder or injury

ai.seo_question: What are the four cases in Shia fiqh where there is no wergild (Diyah) for killing someone?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'no diyah for the aggressor' across four distinct legal scenarios: execution by hadd, self-defense, and punishment for peeping. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the right to compensation is forfeited when the victim is the initiator of the transgression or exceeds legal limits, reinforcing the concept of 'man bada'a fa'tudiyu' (he who starts, is retaliated against).

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Whichever man killed by the legal penalty (Hadd) regarding the retaliation, so there is no wergild for him’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whichever man attacks upon a man, so he defends himself, so he injures him or kills him (in self-defense) so there is nothing upon him’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whichever man looks upon a people in their houses, in order to look at their nakedness, so they pelt him, so it blinds his eye, or injures it, so there is no wergild for him’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who initiates (an attack), so he is attacked against, so there is no retaliation for him’.
